summary.value: The Asil, also spelled Aseel, is an old game fowl from the Indian subcontinent, bred there for fighting for well over 2,000 years. Its name comes from an Arabic word for purebred. The bird is compact and very muscular, with short hard feathers held tight to the body, an upright stance, yellow legs, a small pea comb and a hooked beak. It looks lighter than it is. US standards put cocks at about 6 pounds and hens near 5, while Indian village birds can run heavier. Hens lay very few eggs, often under 70 a year and sometimes far fewer, small and cream to light brown. They are superb broody hens and fierce mothers. Asils fight other chickens, even as chicks, but many bond well with their keepers. They handle heat and range well. This is a bird for experienced keepers, not beginners.
